history.summary: The Bannari Amman Temple stands on NH 209 at Bannari, ~15 km from Sathyamangalam and ~65 km from Erode, at the foot of the Western Ghats near the Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve. The presiding Bannari Mariamman is a swayambumurthi (self-manifested) form of Shakti who faces west. Legend says the goddess protected traders from Tamil Nadu who carried goods by cattle-back along the forest path to Mysore; enchanted by the spot's beauty she chose to stay and bless pilgrims. The Dananayakkan/Dhandanyakkan forest took the name Bannari from the shrine. The shrine began as a shed roofed with the forest herb 'Kanangu', then gained tiled roofs and a gopuram over the sanctum through villagers' efforts; the Shobhana Mandapam with 24 carved pillars was built in 1967, alongside the Artha and Maha Mandapams. Unusually, ant-hill sand - not sacred vibhuti - is given as prasad. A British forest official who barred villagers from cutting forest wood for the Kundam festival is said to have fallen ill with vomiting and diarrhoea until he relented and was cured by the temple's holy ash and water. The famous Kundam fire-walk festival in Panguni (March-April) draws lakhs of devotees.

name: Bannari Amman Temple (Arulmigu Bannari Mariamman Temple)
town: Bannari, Sathyamangalam taluk (CSV town 'Erode' is approximate - ~65 km from the city)
town_description: Bannari is a village on NH 209 in Sathyamangalam taluk, Erode district, at the base of the Western Ghats near the Sathyamangalam forests. It is one of Tamil Nadu's most famous Amman pilgrimage sites, on the Mysore highway where buses between Coimbatore/Erode and Chamarajanagar/Mysore pass through.

travel.railway: Mettupalayam (~nearest, verify); other options Coimbatore and Chamarajanagar
travel.road: On NH 209, 15 km from Sathyamangalam; buses from Sathyamangalam, Erode, Gobichettipalayam and Coimbatore to Mysore/Chamarajanagar/Kollegal pass through Bannari; special buses run on Sundays, Mondays, Fridays and new-moon days

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Panguni (March-April) for the Kundam festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:30 PM and 4:30-8:30 PM per one guide; other sources say 5:30 AM-9:00 PM or 6:00 AM-8:30 PM (conflict - verify)
